claims.text: The combined closed-loop dynamic laser-power and localized LN2-cooling intervention will reduce residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The intervention will refine the microstructure of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The intervention will enhance the mechanical properties of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components relative to conventional high-energy-input processing.
The AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is high-purity and spherical.
The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock inherently has high residual stresses caused by rapid solidification under conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
A laser-power window of approximately 150–250 W and scan-speed window of 600–900 mm/s is applicable to the proposed processing of miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
A synchronized LN2 gas jet can maintain the substrate or powder temperature well below the melting point during the proposed laser process.
The intervention will produce a refined, near-equilibrium microstructure.
The intervention will minimize the formation of microstructural defects.
Localized LN2 cooling reduces the thermal gradient during laser melting.
Real-time thermal-imaging-guided laser-power modulation optimizes energy input.
Combining LN2 cooling with dynamic laser-power modulation lowers peak temperatures.
Combining LN2 cooling with dynamic laser-power modulation reduces thermal-cycling intensity.
Lower peak temperatures and reduced thermal cycling decrease residual-stress accumulation.
The proposed thermal control promotes homogenized microstructural evolution.
The intervention will increase microhardness relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The intervention will improve tensile strength relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The intervention will eliminate the need for multistep post-process heat treatments.
Conventional high-energy-input additive manufacturing without in-situ cooling or dynamic laser modulation produces higher residual stresses.
Conventional high-energy-input additive manufacturing without in-situ cooling or dynamic laser modulation produces degraded mechanical properties.
